institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nature, relevant courses, active student life, price of exchange

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't remember any.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No showing around, that would have been nice or more study specific social introduction

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult, it took quite a bit of effort.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are very nice, but not that tidy and you should not expect very social housing situations.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember, but it involved a lot of different login information like emails, pins, several passwords, user names and digits to resemble a norwegian D-number which was a lot of information to keep track of.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They answered pretty quick to questions on email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful, but a lot of errors in their system with old courses that did not run anymore.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep track of all login information from the beginning in a note or document.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses were good but none as high quality as courses in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was mostly not very high level just low quality of teaching making it a lot of self study. But exams were very easy to pass in general. One course propably exceeded 7,5 ects in amount of content but otherwise it corresponded well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a lot less colloquia style teaching, it was just lectures. I missed the practical aspect of laboratory work that we often have at UCPH and I really missed teacher directed colloquia of content in the course. n

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Immunology, Medical bacteriology, Nanomedicine 1 and introduction to pharmacology.,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Immunology was interesting and covered a lot of relevant topics. Pharmacology was very easy to pass and although they sometimes mixed up languages and some things were in norwegian it was a nice look into the process of pharmacology and drug development.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Lots of nice trips

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The trips arranged specifically for exchange students were very expensive, but all types of sports in NTNUI were pretty cheap to sign up for. Their trips were also cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of things arranged by ESN Trondheim both social and cultural. Samfundet arranges a lot of social and cultural events. NTNUI offers a lot of athletic activities and also social activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Using NTNUI especially their Koie network with lots of small cabins you can stay in for very cheap.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: They should see part of vestlandet, maybe dovrefjellet which is not far and if possible visit Lofoten in some part of the off season for the beautiful nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It is very similar to Denmark in many ways.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn norwegian and try to speak it yourself, it will make you a lot easier to understand for norwegians.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hmm not any in particular. n

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their tradition for friluftsliv and going out in nature in all types of weather,

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Learn norwegian, try to find housing with norwegians who want to be social and make sure to enjoy the nature at any opportunity both close to Trondheim and further away,

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Find housing early as it can be difficult. Use both facebook and
hybel.no
and make sure to find housing that's not above 6000 nok pr month. There are many cheaper options and there will a lot of more fun ways to spend your money.,

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the nature with new friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The darkness. Especially in the exam period.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
